title: DHS OIG Mandates Revision Act of 2014
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on September 16, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

DHS OIG Mandates Revision Act of 2014 - Repeals requirements that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Inspector General: (1) conduct an annual evaluation of the Cargo Inspection Targeting System pursuant to the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Act of 2004, (2) conduct an annual review of Coast Guard Performance pursuant to the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (HSA), and (3) conduct an annual review of grants to states and high-risk urban areas under HSA.

summary.headline: A 2014 law removes three yearly review duties that the Department of Homeland Security's Inspector General had been required to perform.
summary.what_it_does: The law repeals three recurring requirements for the Department of Homeland Security's Inspector General, the office that audits and oversees the department. The first was an annual evaluation of the Cargo Inspection Targeting System, a tool used to pick shipping containers for inspection. The second was an annual review of Coast Guard performance. The third was an annual review of grants that the department gives to states and high-risk urban areas. After this law, the Inspector General no longer has to do these three reviews every year.

who_it_affects.group: DHS Office of Inspector General staff
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to carry out these three annual reviews, which frees up their work schedule.
The yearly outside review of the cargo targeting system is no longer required, though the system itself is not changed by this law.

who_it_affects.group: State and local governments and high-risk urban areas that receive DHS grants
who_it_affects.how: The yearly federal oversight review of their DHS grants is no longer required under this law.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on December 18, 2014.
